ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening is required before incorporation and before opening any French bank account. All UBOs, gérants, delegates, and financial backers must be checked against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) OFAC SDN and SSI Lists for USD payment rails; (iv) the French national financial sanctions list administered by the Direction générale du Trésor; and (v) FATF and Republic of France high-risk third-country lists. PEP definitions follow Articles R.561-18 and R.561-19 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. Positive matches require refusal or enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds evidence, and approval by the designated AML compliance officer; suspicious activity is reported to Tracfin.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités Entreprises (guichet-entreprises.inpi.fr); Infogreffe/RCS name search portal (infogreffe.fr); INPI data repository (data.inpi.fr) for trademark conflicts.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SARL's statutory name (dénomination sociale) must be stated in the articles of association and in all legal documents, invoices and commercial paper. The name may contain foreign-language words but must be in Latin alphabet script; non-Latin names must be transliterated. All statutory and RCS filings must be in French, or accompanied by a certified French translation. The name must be followed or preceded by the words 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' and the amount of share capital. French-language requirements under the Loi Toubon apply to compulsory company information.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: chambre de commerce / chamber of commerce
France republic-related tokens unless legally non-misleading and approved
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not maintain a legally binding prior name reservation system; the 30-day window represents the standard validity and re-check period for a name-availability due-diligence clearance, including RCS, trademark and domain-name conflict checks. If the proposed name is rejected by the RCS/Guichet Unique or challenged on trademark grounds, the applicant should: (i) amend the name and resubmit the incorporation file through the Guichet Unique; (ii) if the registry formalities are refused, file a written appeal within 30 days before the registry supervisory judge (juge commis à la surveillance du registre du tribunal de commerce); and (iii) in parallel, initiate an interim injunction (référé) before the competent commercial court or tribunal judiciaire if a prior trademark owner blocks the name. The same appeal route applies to UBO declaration rejections and RCS registration refusals.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted under Article L.123-11-1 and R.123-211 of the French Commercial Code, subject to use of an approved domiciliation company (domiciliataire agréé) or a valid lease. A pure equity-holding SPV may use an administrative virtual office for statutory domicile, but it must maintain actual substance in France: effective management decisions, accounting records, meeting minutes, and a registered agent empowered to receive process. A mail-only letterbox without any local decision-taking function is not permissible and may trigger tax-residency and anti-abuse challenges.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 20–25% annual probability for a passive holding SPV at incorporation stage. The likelihood increases to approximately 35% if the French tax administration opens a corporate audit, if UBO jurisdictions raise European or international sanctions risk, or if the company files distributions inconsistent with economic substance. Unannounced on-site inspections are legally available under Article L.16B of the French Book of Tax Procedures and may be exercised by the tax police on an exceptional basis.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title III, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 for SARL; general formation provisions in Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10; registration provisions in R.210-1 et seq.; Civil Code Articles 1832 to 1844-9 as the general legal basis of the company contract.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (competent Commercial Court Registry) as administrator of the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE), with filings received through the Guichet Unique operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company creation file (formalité de création d'entreprise) submitted to the RNE via the Guichet Unique, comprising the signed articles of association, capital deposit certificate, legal announcement certificate and statutory beneficial-owner declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for a French SARL. Cash contributions must be deposited with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations in the name of the company in formation; the registry accepts the bank capital-deposit certificate as proof. At formation at least 20% of each cash share's nominal value must be paid, with the balance payable within five years; in-kind contributions must be fully paid on incorporation. For this passive equity-holding SPV, fully paid-up capital is strongly recommended to satisfy bank AML/KYC requirements and to simplify release of blocked deposits after issuance of the Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the Founding Shareholders approve the share capital of [capital amount] divided into [number] equal shares; the subscriptions, contributions and bank capital-deposit certificate are ratified; and any in-kind contributions have been fully paid and vested in the SARL. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the registered office be fixed at [address], France, which shall be the statutory seat, place of central administration and service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER: that [name] be and is hereby appointed First Manager for an indefinite term, with full powers to open bank accounts, subscribe and file all formation documents, publish the legal notice, and obtain the Kbis registration evidencing incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Articles of Association and Prepare Shareholder KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique / INPI and Greffe records for name availability checks; a notaire in the department of the registered office where notarization is required; internal incorporation counsel otherwise.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the corporate name, share capital, equal shares, corporate purpose restricted to passive equity holding, registered office, first manager, accounting year and authorized representatives. Have all shareholders and the first manager sign the articles and manager acceptance; notarization is required only where a contribution is made of real property or assets subject to public registration. Prepare the beneficial-owner declaration and gather shareholder identity, address, source-of-funds and tax residence documentation for bank and registry AML purposes.
required_dossiers: Draft and final private or notarized articles of association
Written acceptance of office signed by the first manager
Identity documents and proof of address of each shareholder and manager
Declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs)
In-kind contribution valuation report or commissaire aux apports report when required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry challenges the proposed name or corporate purpose, amend the articles, obtain fresh signatures and resubmit through the same Guichet Unique file. If an in-kind valuation is defective, commission a corrected report or restructure the contribution as cash.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Share Capital and Obtain Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the capital-deposit certificate is a private instrument, not registered with the state.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company in formation and transfer the cash subscriptions from each shareholder. The bank issues a certificate of deposit stating the intended company name, amount received, French registered office address and beneficiary. For in-kind contributions, execute the transfer deed and obtain the statutory valuation report. Keep the capital blocked until registration unless the articles or the mandate lawfully permit early release for incorporation expenses.
required_dossiers: Certificate of deposit of funds issued by the bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
Reference of each cash transfer from the shareholders
In-kind contribution transfer deed and valuation report
Draft articles reproducing the capital and subscription allocations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a mismatch in company name, capital or shareholder identity, request immediate reissuance from the bank before filing. If the bank refuses the account for AML reasons, provide source-of-wealth documentation and the passive holding structure chart, or approach another French credit institution.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SARL entities obtain SIREN/SIRET from INSEE and register for TVA/VAT ID on impots.gouv.fr; foreign entities must establish French tax residency and apply for identification number through the same DGFiP process
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; subject to French corporate tax regime with hybrid mismatch adjustments under ATAD

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory Factur-X e-invoicing for B2B transactions above thresholds; real-time fiscal clearance via PEPES for large taxpayers; digital invoice stamping required

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods outside the EU and eligible cross-border services to non-EU customers; eligibility requires proof of export and non-EU destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties up to 40% of claimed VAT plus interest; retrospective clawback of zero-rated VAT and potential criminal prosecution for fraudulent claims

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) acting in coordination with the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) and under the prudential framework of the European Central Bank and the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a full Eurozone member and applies the principle of full euro convertibility for both current account and capital account transactions. Under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 63-66 TFEU) and the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), cross-border payments and capital movements are fully liberalized for EU/EEA residents and are subject to no general exchange control authorization. Profit distributions and dividend remittances by a French SARL to its non-French shareholders are permitted without prior Bank of France approval. Non-EU/EEA transfers may be subject merely to statistical declaration and, in limited cases, to due diligence to enforce EU sanctions or detect irregular financial flows. There is no crown-currency restriction on the holding of bank accounts outside France for French-resident entities, but the SARL must report its cross-border financial flows to the Banque de France when mandated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement. No mandatory repatriation timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio exist for export receipts. A French exporter or international equity holding entity may retain export proceeds in foreign currency, either onshore in an authorized French bank account or offshore in a fully compliant foreign bank account. However, cross-border payments exceeding €12,500 in value are subject to the French balance-of-payments reporting regime, which requires the entity or the intermediary bank to complete the appropriate statistical declaration (via the Banque de France). Such reporting requirements are declarative and do not constitute exchange control approval, conversion mandates, or surrender obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_account_regime_summary: Capital account liberalization under EU law is fully applicable. Equity subscriptions, capital contributions, acquisitions, and disposal of participations are freely permitted for EU/EEA investors. Non-EU direct investment may be screened under France's foreign investment control regime only in sensitive sectors, but such screening does not affect general currency convertibility or non-sensitive equity holding treasury operations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Corporate Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Corporate Account
Operational Corporate Account and Liquidity Management Account
Operational Corporate Account and Cash Pooling Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for licensed EU/EEA Electronic Money Institutions and Payment Institutions passporting into France, and Low for offshore third-country digital EMIs. EU-licensed EMIs such as Qonto, Treezor, or Mangopay can provide French-domiciled payment services and operational euro accounts for treasury movement, but they are not full credit institutions and cannot provide credit facilities, overdrafts, or custody of capital-market instruments. An offshore EMI regulated outside the EEA cannot lawfully carry out payment services or hold funds for a French SARL without obtaining an ACPR-licensed branch or agent arrangement. Completeness of treasury, interbank clearing access, and capacity to handle high-value cross-border capital injections remain materially weaker in digital EMIs; therefore, the primary cross-border banking and clearing relationship should be with a Tier-1 Eurozone credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SARL classified as a medium-risk passive holding SPV, French banks almost universally require an in-person interview with at least one authorised signatory or ultimate beneficial owner at the time of account opening. The interview may take place in France or from a branch of the same banking group abroad, but remote opening is permitted only under conditions set by each bank's ACPR-approved KYC framework, typically with enhanced video-identification, notarised corporate documents, and prior positive reputation. French law itself does not mandatorily require physical presence, but the bank's risk-based KYC policies will likely require that the managing director (gérant) or an appointed legal representative appear physically before the account-opening committee, especially where ultimate shareholders are non-residents or offshore entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a non-European or high-risk nationality resident in a tax-haven or FATF-listed jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Government-issued photo ID, proof of physical residential address, full UBO declaration in the French STR registers (TCF/INPI), notarised explanation of source of wealth, audited shareholder financial statements, tax residence certificates, and any necessary OFAC/ACPR sanctions screening reports demonstrating clearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pure equity holding SPV with no operating activity, no staff, and no bespoke board minutes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Strategic group explanatory memorandum, SARL by-laws with non-trading holding object, board resolution approving the banking relationship, organisational chart, audited or carefully prepared pro-forma accounts showing the treasury role, evidence of passive income streams, and an economic substance and tax compliance note evidencing French tax coverage and directors' oversight.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital contribution from a related shareholder or parent without auditable trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised share subscription agreement or capital increase deed, parent board minutes approving the financing, audited parent accounts, banking reference of the parent, wire transfer instruction with explicit purpose code, and sworn declaration from the SARL's legal representative that the transaction reflects a lawful equity investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Significant beneficial ownership layered through multiple opaque foreign holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extracts from every jurisdiction in the ownership chain, notarised translations into French or English, organisational charts certified by directors, register of beneficial owners (if any), legal opinion from a licensed international law firm confirming transparency and lawful source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP (politically exposed person) status of any officer, shareholder, or family member
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Self-certification and questionnaire of the competent compliance department, wealth origin documentation including tax returns and asset titles, details of the underlying commercial rationale, notarised declarations from all PEP-related individuals, unqualified references from two independent regulated financial institutions, and enhanced monitoring consent.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.banking_relationship_risk_mitigation: The SARL should appoint a resident French individual or qualified French corporate service provider as authorized local representative if the non-resident officers cannot appear. This reduces onboarding friction and provides the bank with a verifiable point of contact, although ultimate signatory authority remains per the SARL's article of incorporation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound protocols: (1) The parent/shareholder must transmit a cross-border SWIFT MT103 wire from its own established bank account; (2) the wire must be in EUR for direct settlement on TARGET2, or in an acceptable convertible currency for conversion in France; (3) the payment beneficiary is the French SARL's account held at the receiving French Tier-1 bank; (4) the purpose of payment must be encoded as “Capital Subscription / Equity Contribution” or the Banque de France balance-of-payments category “Investissement direct / Capital social - prise de participation”; (5) the bank must receive and register the supporting corporate resolution of the SARL authorising the capital increase or equity injection and the corresponding shareholder resolution; (6) all transaction documents must be originals or certified true copies and must be retained for the Bank's AML file; (7) if the amount triggers French balance-of-payments statistical reporting, either the receiving bank or the SARL must file the appropriate declaration (type DOP or DY/OIP) with the Banque de France; (8) if the foreign contribution exceeds France's European sanctions threshold, full automatic sanctions screening happens both at the correspondent and the receiving bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The passive equity holding SARL is expected to make recurring outbound payments for group management fees, interest payments, legal fees, future acquisition consideration, dividend remittances to the parent, and repayment of shareholder loans. Acceptable clearing rails are: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR for payment to EU/EEA beneficiaries, using the SARL's IBAN and BIC with mandatory purpose codes; (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA cross-border transfers, carrying the beneficiary bank's BIC, the parent's IBAN or account number, and precise payment details; (3) Trade settlement is not normally performed by a holding SPV, but if a purchase of subsidiary shares requires a documentary payment, the SARL may use a Standard Documentary Letter of Credit (UCP600), unwritten or standby LC, or a Bank Payment Obligation (BPO) only when its bank approves the underlying commercial contract; (4) for truly commercial cost disbursements, direct debits via SEPA Direct Debit are available for recurrent Swiss, French, and euro-area payments after supplier mandate verification. Dividends to the holding parent are settled via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA transfer after the corporate distribution approval and the relevant taxd withholding declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward contracts with an authorised French or EEA credit institution to hedge anticipated dividend remittances and capital movements into or out of EUR

FX Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF), permissible only where the underlying trade/investment currency is non-convertible or restricted, and executed through an international clearing bank or ACPR-authorised foreign exchange market-maker
FX Swap with a French banking counterparty for short-term treasury conversion between EUR and foreign currencies, provided the settlement is documentary and included in the treasury policy
Currency Option (purchased call or put) to protect disbursement budgets or acquisition currency exposure, subject to the bank's ISDA and Credit Support Annex framework
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.additional_clearing_scheme_details: For large-value euro clearing, the Banque de France operates TARGET2 and the European Central Bank's T2 payment system. For lower-value recurring payments, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) is available with a French bank account, enabling almost instantaneous treasury moves in euros. The French SARL must maintain at least one operational euro account in France to access TARGET2 and SEPA. For US Dollar denominated flows, correspondent US clearing may be through a US-dollar nostro account at the French bank's correspondent in the United States, using CHIPS or Fedwire as final transfer rails.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements (Bilan and Compte de Résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15th day of the 4th month following the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of up to 0.5% of annual turnover per month of delay, potential administrative dissolution after 3 months of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing by 31 January or within 30 days of any change in UBO
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €5,000 and potential strike-off for non-compliance with beneficial ownership requirements

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit if two of the following criteria are met: turnover > €800,000, balance sheet total > €400,000, or average headcount > 50 employees

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation and update of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) register maintained at the RCS, including any shareholding changes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 100-400 USD (typical annual fee for registered office and agent services in France)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0-3,000 USD (typically 0 for holding companies below audit thresholds, otherwise 2,000-5,000 USD)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption for qualifying dividends from subsidiaries under the mère-fille regime

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, financial income and deductible charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All items must be supported by invoices and arm's-length documentation

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Administrative fine of 0.75% of tax due per month of delay (maximum 10%); criminal sanctions for wilful evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% standard rate, reduced by applicable double tax treaty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC application to French tax authorities with supporting documentation and beneficial ownership certificates
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory rate, reduced by treaty (typically 0-10%); Interest: 25% statutory rate, reduced by treaty (typically 0-10%)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable under French implementation of OECD BEPS Action 5; holding companies must demonstrate real economic substance and decision-making in France

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable profits or submission of false tax declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to 80% of evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, restitution orders and potential imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file or late submission of corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of 0.75% per month of delay on tax due (maximum 10%)
